title: Taiwan-morning overnight cross-asset price, news and actual-flow evidence

as_of.cutoff_control: All quoted prices and article timestamps were filtered to or were published before the 2026-10-12T01:12:00Z cutoff. Traditional-market official closes and ETF creations/redemptions use the latest available completed business date, 2026-10-09, unless otherwise stated.

assets: US Treasury yields and Treasury futures
scope.flow_scope: Source-reported creations/redemptions or holdings changes for physically backed gold ETFs and US spot BTC/ETH ETFs. Price changes are never treated as flows.

methodology_and_controls: Separated price/yield observations, news/catalyst reporting, and actual ETF-flow evidence.
Used exact source observation dates and times where available; used the last completed one-minute candle ending before the cutoff for Coinbase crypto prices.
For traditional markets, distinguished the latest official Friday close from Monday Asian-hours futures/index indications.

For ETF flows, used the latest available trading date (Friday 2026-10-09) for US spot crypto ETFs and the latest World Gold Council monthly dataset (2026-09-30) for gold ETFs; there are no Saturday/Sunday creation-redemption rows.
No causal claim is made solely from contemporaneous co-movement.
executive_findings: Monday Asian-hours indications showed gold futures higher, the DXY slightly lower, and 10-year Treasury-note futures slightly higher than their prior closes, while BTC and ETH were both higher over the previous 24 hours.
The latest official US Treasury curve was still restrictive: 10-year nominal 5.24% and 10-year real 2.91% on 2026-10-09.
Reuters' Monday Asia market wrap described cautious risk appetite, high bond yields and continued Fed-tightening risk; it also quoted spot gold up 0.3% near USD 4,206/oz and DXY near 102.25.

Actual ETF flows were mixed and stale relative to weekend crypto trading: on 2026-10-09 US spot BTC ETFs had +USD 21.1m while spot ETH ETFs had -USD 56.1m. For the full 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-09 week, computed from Farside daily rows, BTC ETFs had -USD 678.9m and ETH ETFs -USD 542.2m.

The latest World Gold Council dataset was monthly, not daily: global physically backed gold ETFs attracted about USD 10bn in September 2026, added 67 tonnes, and reached record holdings of 4,256 tonnes as of 2026-09-30.
ETH outperformed BTC modestly over the measured 24 hours: ETH/BTC rose about 0.44% to 0.030335. This is relative price performance, not evidence of capital flow into ETH.

price_evidence.instrument: COMEX gold futures continuous contract proxy (Yahoo Finance GC=F)
price_evidence.note: Futures contract proxy; not identical to spot gold. Yahoo's last source-stamped observation before the 09:12 Taipei cutoff was 09:04:48.

reported_factors: Cautious Asian risk tone ahead of earnings season.
US Treasury yields remained near multi-decade highs after the prior week's rise.
Fed officials had warned of further tightening and markets assigned material probability to rate increases.
Thin liquidity because Japan was closed and the US had a partial holiday.
news_and_catalysts.interpretation: Gold rose even with the dollar still near a 17-month high. The simultaneous Monday dip in DXY and rise in Treasury-note futures are directionally supportive, but this report does not prove either caused the gold move.

reported_factors: Softer dollar and easing Treasury yields supported gold early in the latest completed US session.
Markets were focused on US CPI and the next Federal Reserve decision.
The dollar later reversed higher, capping gold's advance.

actual_etf_flow_evidence.frequency: monthly latest available World Gold Council data
actual_etf_flow_evidence.control_note: This is verified fund-flow/holdings evidence, not inferred from gold's price. It is monthly and must not be described as a 2026-10-09 or weekend flow. WGC explicitly noted that holdings rose despite a lower September gold price, illustrating price/flow divergence.

price_evidence.instrument: US Dollar Index as quoted by Reuters
price_evidence.context: near a 17-month high in Monday Asia trading

reported_support: Markets still saw roughly 50-50 odds of a December Fed hike and about a 63% probability of a January move, according to Reuters' Monday wrap.
Fed officials, including St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem, had argued that lowering inflation could require more rate increases.
The dollar had gained about 0.5% the prior week.
reported_near_term_watch: US CPI forecast at 3.3% year-on-year for both headline and core.
US retail sales and producer prices were also due in the week.

actual_flow_evidence.reason: DXY is a price index; there is no single canonical aggregate 'USD ETF flow' corresponding to the index. No flow conclusion is inferred from DXY's move.

official_yield_evidence.note: Official Treasury par-curve closing values. The prior 2026-10-08 10-year nominal and real yields were 5.22% and 2.87%, respectively.

monday_futures_indication.instrument: CBOT 10-year Treasury note futures continuous proxy (Yahoo Finance ZN=F)
monday_futures_indication.interpretation_control: Higher note-futures prices normally point to lower yields, but the futures-price move is not converted here into an unverified spot-yield estimate.

reported_background: Reuters said 10-year and 30-year Treasury yields had touched 24-year highs the prior week.
A Reuters poll expected the 10-year yield to finish 2026 around 5.02%, above September's 4.90% forecast, with analysts flagging 5.5% and then 6% as risks if inflation stayed high and growth firm.
PIMCO CIO Dan Ivascyn said there was a meaningful risk that the 10-year yield could reach 6% within six to twelve months.

actual_etf_flow_evidence.reason: No fund universe was specified for Treasury ETFs and there is no single canonical aggregate Treasury-ETF flow series equivalent to the Farside spot-crypto tables. Yield changes and futures moves are not labeled as flows.

news_and_catalysts.comment: The verified Monday Reuters cross-asset wrap did not attribute the BTC move to a specific fresh headline. The measured price gain is therefore reported without a causal narrative.

actual_us_spot_etf_flows.control_note: The Friday +USD 21.1m is the latest actual creation/redemption-flow aggregate. There is no weekend row; it does not explain or measure Saturday-Sunday BTC trading.

news_and_catalysts.comment: No verified contemporaneous source in this research set tied the ETH move to a fresh weekend headline. The price move is presented independently from ETF flows.

actual_us_spot_etf_flows.control_note: ETH rose 1.56% over the measured weekend 24 hours even though the latest available Friday ETF row was a USD 56.1m outflow. These observations have different timestamps and do not establish causation; notably, they also show why price direction cannot be relabeled as flow.

eth_btc.method: ETH-USD close divided by BTC-USD close on Coinbase for matched one-minute candles
eth_btc.interpretation: ETH modestly outperformed BTC over the matched 24-hour window. This is a relative-price statement only, not evidence of rotation or fund flow.

actual_etf_flow_summary.weekend_data_warning: US ETF primary-market flow tables do not publish Saturday/Sunday rows. All crypto ETF figures are the latest Friday values, not weekend flows. Gold's latest source is monthly, not daily.

cross_asset_read.observed_pattern: By roughly 09:05-09:11 Taipei, gold futures were +0.53% from prior close, DXY -0.10%, 10-year note futures +0.07%, BTC +1.11% over 24h and ETH +1.56% over 24h. This is consistent with mild dollar/rate relief during thin Monday trading, but it is not proof of a common causal flow.
cross_asset_read.macro_tension: The immediate Monday indications were a little friendlier to duration and non-dollar assets, but the latest official 10-year nominal yield of 5.24% and real yield of 2.91%, plus live Fed-hike risk, remained a restrictive backdrop.
cross_asset_read.flow_divergence: Gold's latest monthly ETF inflow occurred despite a lower September gold price, and ETH's weekend price gain followed a Friday ETF outflow. Both examples directly reject a price-equals-flow assumption.
cross_asset_read.relative_crypto: ETH/BTC's +0.44% 24-hour change showed modest ETH outperformance, while latest actual US spot ETF flows still favored BTC on Friday (+USD 21.1m versus ETH -USD 56.1m). Because the timestamps differ, this is contrast, not a rotation claim.

limitations: The Reuters canonical Monday article body was not fully extractable directly; the article's body and timing were cross-checked through syndicated Reuters copies while retaining the canonical Reuters URL.
Yahoo's latest stamped traditional-market observations lagged the requested cutoff by about seven minutes; exact source timestamps are recorded rather than pretending they were 09:12 ticks.
No high-confidence BTC- or ETH-specific breaking-news catalyst was verified inside the weekend window, so none is invented.
Gold ETF flows are latest monthly WGC figures as of 2026-09-30; they are not weekend or 2026-10-09 flows.
No canonical aggregate USD-ETF or Treasury-ETF fund-flow series was established; price and yield changes are not used as substitutes.
